old_row.relationship: Children dashed in judgment against Babylon
old_row.rationale: The psalm’s violent blessing concerning Babylon’s infants corresponds to Isaiah’s Babylon oracle describing their children dashed before them. Isaiah does not specify the psalm’s rock, and the comparison reports the texts rather than extending their command to another setting.

proposed_new_row.relationship: Children dashed in judgment against Babylon
proposed_new_row.rationale: The psalm’s violent blessing concerning Babylon’s infants corresponds to Isaiah’s Babylon oracle describing their children dashed before them. Isaiah does not specify the psalm’s rock.

proposed_changes.reason: The source is a blessing and the target is a prediction; neither retained unit issues the command claimed by the deleted clause.

old_row.rationale: Both passages combine divine holding and guidance. Psalm 138 says God’s right hand holds the speaker; Psalm 72 says God grasped the speaker’s right hand and guided him in counsel.

proposed_new_row.rationale: Both passages combine divine holding and guidance. Psalm 138 says God’s right hand will hold the speaker; Psalm 72 says God grasped the speaker’s right hand and guided him in counsel.

proposed_changes.reason: Preserve the source future while distinguishing the target past grasping and guidance.

old_row.relationship: Divine breath or wind controls frost and water
old_row.rationale: The Lord’s sending His word to melt the ice and blowing wind so waters flow correspond to frost given from the Strong One’s breath and His steering water as He wishes. Frost-giving and melting are different actions.

proposed_new_row.relationship: Divine breath or wind controls frost and water
proposed_new_row.rationale: The Lord’s sending His word to melt the ice and blowing wind so waters flow correspond to Elihu’s description of frost given from the Strong One’s breath and His steering water as He wishes. Frost-giving and melting are different actions.

proposed_changes.reason: The actual Job 32:6, 36:1 and 38:1 speaker markers identify this as Elihu’s speech; state that attribution rather than leave the target voice implicit.

old_row.relationship: Goodness and beauty in the summons to praise
old_row.rationale: Psalm 146 commends praise because a psalm is good and asks that praise please God; Psalm 134 commands praise because the Lord is good and music because His name is beautiful. The differing subjects of good are preserved.

proposed_new_row.relationship: A praise summons with differing goodness clauses
proposed_new_row.rationale: Both summon praise of the Lord and follow it with a goodness clause. Psalm 146 calls a psalm good and asks that praise please God; Psalm 134 calls the Lord good and commands music to His name, adding “for it is beautiful.” The repeated form is compared without equating the subjects of good or resolving the final it.

proposed_changes.reason: Keep the particular repeated praise-and-reason form while preserving different goodness predicates and the supplied final pronoun.

old_case.relationship: Proposed identification of David’s cave occasion
old_case.rationale: The psalm heading names a cave but no location or pursuer. Samuel records David in the En-gedi cave and also records the Adullam cave in 22:1. This target does not uniquely establish the heading’s occasion.
old_case.reason: The psalm heading names a cave but no location or pursuer. Samuel records David in the En-gedi cave and also records the Adullam cave in 22:1. This target does not uniquely establish the heading’s occasion.

proposed_new_case.relationship: Proposed identification of David’s cave occasion
proposed_new_case.rationale: The psalm heading names a cave but no location or pursuer. The account in 1 Samuel records David in the En-gedi cave and also records the Adullam cave in 22:1. This target does not uniquely establish the heading’s occasion.
proposed_new_case.reason: The psalm heading names a cave but no location or pursuer. The account in 1 Samuel records David in the En-gedi cave and also records the Adullam cave in 22:1. This target does not uniquely establish the heading’s occasion.

candidate_changes.reason: Identify the book account without implying personal narrative authorship by Samuel.
